comments.author: Alexander Terp
comments.body:
Answered 2026-09-03 while working slot 2. The position and the click both reach Muster; neither
reaches the program in the pane, and that half is blocked on a_27CTgqqdv rather than missing.

**What reaches Muster.** `SurfaceView.mouseDown` reports the click so the core can move the
keyboard to that pane, and every press, drag and release is forwarded to the pane's own
libghostty surface with the pointer position converted into the surface's coordinates
(`SurfaceView.reportMousePosition`). That is what makes a drag select text and Cmd-C copy it,
and it is why the cell under the pointer is already known accurately - the surface has the same
grid the person is looking at. Selection is now anchored to the pane rather than to a screen
row, which is a_2ADMeD8nM.

**What does not reach the program, and why it is not a plumbing gap.** Nothing sends the click
on to the pane's PTY, deliberately. A program that never enabled mouse reporting receives an
SGR sequence as typed text - garbage in a shell, a corrupted prompt in an agent mid-task - so
the click has to be gated on the mode, and the mode is not readable. Muster's own surface has a
getter for it, `ghostty_surface_mouse_captured`, and it answers `false` for every pane because
herdr's VT consumes the mode-setting sequences before the frame stream ever carries them. The
measurement and the source citations are section 12 of
`docs/observations/libghostty-9f9b8d1d.md`.

The wheel is the exception and is already right: `terminal.scroll` is structured, and the
daemon encodes it against the pane's real state. Buttons and motion have no equivalent, which
is exactly what a_27CTRluw7 asks for.

So this card has its answer and the work behind it is a_27CTgqqdv.
